scope: Proposition 14.4 (Integral rounding) of the manuscript “Bounded klt complements for Fano contractions” (preprints/Bounded-klt-complements-for-Fano-contractions-September-25-2026/Bounded-klt-complements-for-Fano-contractions-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 066 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d50937326c7cb115), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 90-91. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every absolute tolerance σ > 0, a rank increase followed by a bounded integral scaling and rounding of the new parameters changes a small objective bound BOUNDED KLT COMPLEMENTS 91 according to (14.4) enew = K(σ, d)eold + C10σ. Old parameters remain integral and cheap parameters remain zero. The constants for probe and parameter sizes remain uniform at every later fixed scaling.
